independent_validation_note: FALSE, deliberately, and the manifest agrees. On this site independent_validation does not mean "the reference is independent of the tool's code" -- that is what the "benchmarked" tier itself asserts, and it is true here: the reference is a separate Python implementation derived from first principles that shares no code and no numerical route with the page. The flag means "someone other than the author has reviewed this", which is the reserved "verified" tier and requires a validation.review record naming the reviewer, the date, what was reviewed and where the record can be read. There is no such record: this harness is the author's own and no external party has reviewed it, so the flag stays false, as it does on 45 of the 46 tools already at "benchmarked".

promotion.defect_found_and_fixed: FOUND (first run, against the shipped build): the terminal fill time -- a headline output, printed in the report summary sentence and the results table -- depended on tEnd, the simulated time window, which carries no physics. The march nominated its step as tEnd/900, so widening the window coarsened it; once the step exceeded the remaining fill, the whole subsonic approach to equalisation fell inside a single RK4 step and the terminal bisection located the root of that step rather than of the trajectory. Because the mass rate is convex-decreasing on the subsonic leg, the stage average overestimates it and the fill time came out SHORT -- always non-conservative. Measured under-report: 2.0e-4 at the shipped default, 5.6e-3 at a 55x window, 1.2e-2 at 185x, saturating at 4.7 % (air) / 5.4 % (helium) / 7.2 % (subcritical-throughout); a scan over gamma and initial ratio put the worst at 7.8 %. No warning was raised and every case was inside the declared input ranges. The superseded in-page check could not see any of it: its band was the solver's own step, tEnd/900, which grows in proportion to the error it was meant to catch, so no step size could ever fail it. FIXED: the step is now taken from the transient -- a fixed fraction STEP_FRAC = 0.025 of the remaining-fill timescale (m_stop - m)/mdot(m), with a floor of 1e-9 of the initial fill timescale so it cannot collapse to zero on the sqrt-law approach to equalisation, where the terminal event is then crossed and located exactly by bisection. tEnd survives only inside a min() that can REFINE the step so a short window still draws a smooth curve, and can never coarsen it, so no value of tEnd can degrade the answer. Measured after the fix: the reported fill time moves by 1.5e-8 relative across windows from 1.02x to 185000x the fill, against 4.7e-2 to 7.4e-2 before -- an improvement of about six orders of magnitude -- and every terminal time now agrees with the independent reference to between 4e-11 and 1.6e-8.
promotion.also_fixed: Two of the tool's own diagnostics were repaired alongside. (1) The in-page acceptance band for the terminal time was one solver step, tEnd/900; it is now 1e-3 relative, fixed by the model's physical fidelity rather than by its own partition. (2) The in-page mass-domain reference integral stopped 1e-9 of the mass span short of the end to dodge the singular integrand, which silently subtracted the last sliver of the fill -- 6.5e-6 s on the shipped default, larger than the march error the reference exists to measure once the march was fixed. It now integrates in v = sqrt(m_eq - m), which makes the integrand bounded and removes the truncation entirely. The refinement check now grades step-fraction convergence, since there is no window partition left to refine.
promotion.verified: Zero regressions: all 234 checks pass, and of the 226 that already passed, 19 residuals moved and every one of them improved, by three to five orders of magnitude. Four extreme-corner cases at the declared input limits agree with the reference to 5e-10 with no page errors and no step-guard truncation. The exported Python mirrors the new stepper and reproduces the browser result to 1.5e-8 against the reference.

reference: A second implementation, written in Python from an independent first-principles derivation and NOT ported from the page. The mass and energy balances on the rigid adiabatic control volume are closed analytically (m T = m0 T0 + gamma T_s (m - m0)), which makes tank pressure affine in mass and reduces the whole transient to one scalar ODE in the pressure ratio r = p/p_supply. Its choked leg is solved in closed form (the flux is frozen at Shapiro eq. 4.21, so mass rises linearly in time) and its subsonic leg by Gauss-Legendre quadrature in u = sqrt(1-r), a substitution that removes the integrable (1-r)^(-1/2) endpoint singularity exactly. The orifice flux is assembled as rho*w from the isentropic stagnation relations of Shapiro vol. 1 ch. 4, and the choking criterion is anchored to the published p*/p_t = 0.528282 of NACA TR-1135 Table I and to the three-digit SI rule mdot = 0.0404 Cd A p0/sqrt(T0) for air. Real-gas properties from CoolProp (Lemmon et al. air EOS) confirm the gas constants used and quantify the ideal-gas closure error. The reference was verified before use against three structurally different routes (closed form, scipy Radau implicit stiff march, 4e5-node trapezoid), against node refinement, against the analytic near-equalisation asymptote, and by confirming that the tool itself converges onto it as the tool's own step is reduced.
reference_citations: A. H. Shapiro, The Dynamics and Thermodynamics of Compressible Fluid Flow, vol. 1, Ronald Press, New York, 1953 -- ch. 4: steady one-dimensional isentropic flow. Eq. 4.14 (T0/T = 1 + (g-1)/2 M^2) and eq. 4.15 (p0/p = (T0/T)^(g/(g-1))) give the isentropic stagnation relations used to build the orifice mass flux; eq. 4.19 gives the critical pressure ratio p*/p0 = (2/(g+1))^(g/(g-1)); eq. 4.21 gives the choked mass flux per unit area G* = p0 sqrt(g/(R T0)) (2/(g+1))^((g+1)/(2(g-1))). Table B.2 of the same volume tabulates p/p0 = 0.528282 at M = 1 for g = 1.4.

Ames Research Staff, Equations, Tables and Charts for Compressible Flow, NACA Report 1135, 1953 -- eq. (45) and Table I (isentropic flow, g = 1.4): p/p_t = 0.528282 and T/T_t = 0.833333 at M = 1. Used as the published digit-level anchor for the choking criterion.

The SI form of the choked-orifice rule for air, mdot = 0.0404 Cd A p0 / sqrt(T0) (kg/s, m^2, Pa, K) -- the numerical evaluation of Shapiro eq. 4.21 at g = 1.4, R = 287.05 J/(kg K); quoted to three significant figures in the standard relief-sizing literature (e.g. API STD 520 Part I critical-flow coefficient C, and Perry's Chemical Engineers' Handbook, compressible flow through nozzles). Used as an independent three-digit anchor on the tool's peak inlet flow.

E. W. Lemmon, R. T. Jacobsen, S. G. Penoncello, D. G. Friend, "Thermodynamic properties of air and mixtures of nitrogen, argon and oxygen from 60 to 2000 K at pressures to 2000 MPa", J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 29(3), 2000, pp. 331-385 -- reached through CoolProp 8.0 (PropsSI). Used to confirm that the tool's default gas constants and gamma are the real values (R_air = 287.0475 vs 287.05 J/(kg K), gamma_air = 1.40194 at 1 bar/293.15 K vs 1.4; R_He = 2077.264 vs 2077) and to quantify the ideal-gas closure error that sets the physical tolerance floor: Z(air, 293.15 K) = 0.99962 at 1 bar, 0.99362 at 20 bar, 0.98790 at 50 bar.
scipy 1.17 solve_ivp(method='Radau'), Hairer & Wanner's stiffly accurate implicit Runge-Kutta, used as the structurally independent cross-check on the quadrature route.
provenance_note: Independent second implementation (Python 3 / numpy / scipy / CoolProp), generated by bench-src/gen_tank_pressurisation.py; published anchors as cited. Of the 234 graded checks, 231 are recomputed -- by that implementation, run outside the browser, or, for the retained in-page self-checks, by the tool itself -- and 3 are graded against published figures reused as published (NACA TR-1135 Table I p*/p_t = 0.528282 and the three-digit SI rule mdot = 0.0404 Cd A p0/sqrt(T0)), each to half its own last printed digit.
tolerance: algebraic: 1e-12 relative. p, T, rho, admitted mass and the peak inlet flow of an equalised or t = 0 state are CLOSED-FORM in this model: (A) and (B) give m T and p without any integration, and the peak flow of a case that starts choked is Cd A p_s G*/p_s exactly. Two independent double-precision evaluations of a closed form may differ only by round-off, so the band is set at round-off scale. Observed worst case 4e-14. | trajectory: 1e-8 relative. For quantities read off the trajectory at a truncated window the reference must invert a quadrature and the tool must march 900 RK4 steps, and near the equalisation band the isentropic flux is the difference of two nearly equal powers of r, whose condition number is about 1/(1-r) = 1e5 -- so no double-precision evaluation of either side can be trusted below about 1e-11 relative. 1e-8 leaves three decades over that floor and is still four decades tighter than any physical claim the model can support. Observed worst case 1.6e-9. | time: 1e-3 relative (absolute floor 1e-6 s). The ideal-gas closure this whole model rests on is itself 0.64 % wrong in density at the shipped default's 20 bar supply (CoolProp/Lemmon et al. air EOS, Z = 0.99362 at 293.15 K), so a time-integration error is only defensible while it stays an order of magnitude inside the model's own physical fidelity. 1e-3 does that, and is still about five times looser than the two decimal places at which the page prints the elapsed time in its report. It is NOT derived from the solver's own step, which is the mistake the superseded in-page tolerance made: tEnd/900 grows with the window, so no step size could ever fail it. | published6: 1e-6 relative: half of the last digit of p*/p_t = 0.528282 as published in NACA TR-1135 Table I. | published3: 1.25e-3 relative: half of the last digit of the three-significant-figure published rule mdot = 0.0404 Cd A p0 / sqrt(T0) for air. | window-invariance: 1e-6 relative spread. The time a vessel takes to fill is fixed by the vessel, the orifice and the two gas states; the length of the window the user asks to see is not one of them and must not enter the answer at all. The only admissible spread is the residual discretisation error of the march, which the transient-sized step bounds at about 2e-8 across the whole range tested, so 1e-6 leaves two decades of headroom while still being 4.7e4 times tighter than the 4.7e-2 spread the previous window-derived step produced. Note that this band is derived from the INVARIANCE ITSELF -- a property the physics demands exactly -- and not from any step size, which is what makes it a criterion a bad stepper cannot satisfy. | flux-conditioning: max(1e-12, 100 eps / (1 - r)) relative, evaluated per case from that case's pressure ratio. The isentropic mass flux is a difference of two nearly equal quantities as r -> 1, so its relative condition number is about 1/(1-r) and no double-precision evaluation on either side can be trusted below that floor. At r = 0.06 the band is the 1e-12 round-off minimum; at the 0.99999 equalisation band it is 2.2e-9. The band follows from the expression, not from either implementation.
grading: total counts every check with an acceptance criterion. 219 of them are INDEPENDENT (graded against the Python second implementation described in "reference" and against published compressible-flow data); 15 are SELF-CHECKS retained verbatim from the superseded in-page benchmark, which re-evaluate the tool's own relations inside the tool and therefore do not count as independent reference checks. Cases keep the ids, notes and verdicts they were recorded with.

not_benchmarked: Real-gas behaviour. The state relation is ideal-gas throughout. CoolProp on the Lemmon et al. air equation of state gives Z = 0.99362 at 20 bar / 293.15 K and Z = 1.02601 at 200 bar, so the closure is 0.6 % to 2.6 % wrong in density across the cases run here; the reference shares the ideal-gas closure and so cannot test it.
Vessel-wall heat capacity and wall heat transfer.
Supply-line inventory, regulator dynamics, and mixing stratification: the supply state is held fixed on both sides.

The 0.99999 p_supply equalisation cut-off is a declared model parameter of the tool, taken as an input by the reference rather than tested by it. The true equalisation time is finite (the singularity is integrable) but the reported figure depends on where the band is drawn.
Orifice discharge coefficient Cd. It is a user input on both sides; no measured orifice data is used.
The drawn pressure/temperature history. Only the terminal record is machine-readable, so the trajectory is sampled by truncating the window instead.
notes: Independent cases are graded by a Python second implementation that shares no code and no numerical route with the page. The page was read only for input names, units, declared assumptions and reported quantities.

The trajectory is graded by running the same physics with the window truncated at six times between 2 s and 54 s, which samples p(t), T(t) and m(t) on both the choked and the subsonic leg of the shipped default.

The superseded in-page benchmark accepted the terminal time within one of the solver's own steps, tEnd/900. That band grows with the simulation window, so no step size could ever fail it. This artifact replaces it with a band fixed by the model's physical fidelity.
